competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Comply with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector in all aspects of data/AI use.
Discuss ethical concerns with appropriate individuals or channels and seek guidance for ethical/privacy issues.
Identify and report ethical concerns when appropriate.
Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Consult responsible AI resources.
Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.

indicators: Apply deep learning modeling approaches to solve problems.

competencies.description: Business acumen in data science refers to the ability to understand and apply knowledge of business operations, strategy, and decision-making processes. It involves identifying business needs, aligning data-driven insights with organizational goals, and making decisions that drive organizational success.
indicators: Collaborate with business teams to identify key business objectives and tailor data science projects to align with those objectives.
Assess the potential impact of data science solutions on business performance and communicate how the findings can influence business decisions.
Conduct market research or competitive analysis to understand industry trends and incorporate relevant external data into business decisions.
Work with cross-functional teams (e.g., marketing, finance, product) to ensure data projects are aligned with business priorities.
Tie visualizations explicitly to business rationale and intended use.

competencies.description: Project Management in the context of data science involves planning, organizing, and overseeing data-driven projects from initiation to completion. It includes managing resources, timelines, and deliverables while ensuring that project goals align with business objectives. It also involves risk management, stakeholder communication, and iterative problem-solving throughout the project lifecycle.
indicators: Independently manage smaller, less complex tasks within a project, ensuring deadlines and deliverables are met.
Monitor the progress of data science projects, ensuring the team stays on track, and adjust when necessary (e.g., reallocating resources or extending deadlines).
Identify and mitigate moderate risks in data science projects, including technical issues, resource shortages, or data availability concerns.
Provide regular updates to stakeholders on the status of the project, ensuring clear communication of timelines, issues, and changes.
Engage with users to collect feedback/data during idea/solution implementation.
Engage in evidence-building activities throughout the project cycle.
Flag AI/data governance issues.
Adjust work based on continuous user feedback.
Register new AI solutions/projects with appropriate stakeholders.

competencies.description: Data processing refers to the collection, cleaning, transformation, and manipulation of raw data into a format suitable for analysis and decision-making. It involves handling data from various sources, ensuring its quality, and making it ready for statistical analysis or machine learning models.
indicators: Combine multiple datasets from different sources using joins or merges based on common keys, handling inconsistencies in data structure.
Write scripts to automate common data cleaning tasks, such as removing duplicates, correcting data types, and normalizing values.
Process both structured data (e.g., databases, spreadsheets) and unstructured data (e.g., text, logs) for analysis.
Perform complex data manipulations and transformations (e.g., data aggregation, time series processing).
Specify needs regarding tools and infrastructure requirements (e.g., compute capacity).
Create and maintain structured metadata; cleaning and manipulating structured metadata.
Publish data in machine-readable format.
Review and analyze outliers and their role as a potential root cause for quality issues.
Retain/maintain original data for outcome comparison.
Prioritize high-value datasets for interoperability.
Provide transparent documentation and rationale for dataset fitness for use.
Apply agentic AI tools (e.g., LLMs, workflow orchestrators) to automate data ingestion, cleaning, and transformation.

competencies.description: Knowledge and ability to design, define, construct, enhance, support, and maintain software associated with machine learning.
indicators: Design and implement functions and classes in Python or R, applying object-oriented programming principles.
Use libraries like Pandas, NumPy, or dplyr to perform data manipulation tasks such as cleaning, transforming, and aggregating data.
Write and implement basic unit tests and functions for quality assurance.
Provide drill down functionality in visualizations.

competencies.description: Knowledge in a range of mathematical and statistical techniques, understanding and being able to apply them, and comprehending their underlying assumptions and limitations.
indicators: Apply inferential statistics such as hypothesis testing (t-tests, chi-square tests), confidence intervals, and p-values to draw conclusions from sample data.
Perform and interpret simple linear regression, including understanding the relationship between dependent and independent variables.
Apply techniques for uncovering patterns in data through visualizations and basic statistical analysis, including correlation and scatter plots.
Perform basic multivariate statistical techniques, such as multiple linear regression or principal component analysis (PCA), to handle multiple variables.
Understand the pros and cons of various statistical tests and when they should be applied.

competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

The GC Data Demo Library is a collection of data showcase videos highlighting innovations from across the GC data community for data conference 2023. They demonstrate the power of data to inform better policies, programs and operations. Cutting edge technologies that draw on the power of data, artificial intelligence, and machine learning help the public service innovate and remain relevant as an institution Canadians look to for excellent service, support, and Leadership. As these technologies crunch numbers, summarize data, and process transactions, they provide new opportunities and avenues for public servants to focus on strategic and creative elements in ways never seen before. 

This video series explores how organizations across the federal government are using the power of data, artificial intelligence and machine learning to help the public service innovate and broaden their use moving forward.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Comply with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector in all aspects of data/AI use.
Discuss ethical concerns with appropriate individuals or channels and seek guidance for ethical/privacy issues.
Identify and report ethical concerns when appropriate.
Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Consult responsible AI resources.
Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.

competencies.description: Knowledge and ability to design, define, construct, enhance, support, and maintain software associated with machine learning.
indicators: Write basic programs that include variables, loops, conditionals, and functions to perform simple data tasks.
Use basic data structures such as lists, arrays, and dictionaries to store and manipulate data.
Recognize and correct common programming errors, such as syntax and logical mistakes.
Manipulate data using built-in functions and libraries (e.g., Python's Pandas or R's dplyr).
Use at least one open-source programming language, typically Python or R, for basic data manipulation and analysis tasks.
Consider use of open source over commercial tools.

competencies.description: Data processing refers to the collection, cleaning, transformation, and manipulation of raw data into a format suitable for analysis and decision-making. It involves handling data from various sources, ensuring its quality, and making it ready for statistical analysis or machine learning models.
indicators: Load datasets from common formats (CSV, Excel, SQL) and perform basic cleaning tasks such as handling missing values and formatting issues.
Apply data transformations such as filtering, aggregating, and sorting to prepare data for analysis.
Derive variables to enhance data analysis.
Apply methods to handle missing data (e.g., drop missing records).
Describe the stages of the full data lifecycle (plan, collect, process, use, share, dispose).

competencies.description: The Artificial Intelligence Techniques competency encompasses the knowledge and skills required to develop, deploy, and manage AI-driven solutions, including machine learning algorithms, deep learning models, natural language processing (NLP), and generative AI systems. It covers the full AI pipeline from data preparation and model development to ethical considerations and model deployment.
indicators: Apply deep learning modeling approaches to solve problems.
Apply AI techniques to real-world business problems, demonstrating the ability to develop AI-powered solutions and research.
Fine-tune models and evaluate performance using appropriate metrics (e.g., accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score).
Fine-tune generative AI processes and LLMs.
Recognize the ethical implications of AI, focusing on fairness, bias reduction, and trust in AI design.
Identify AI/data science trends and tools.
Use prompt engineering to guide AI agents in performing structured data tasks.
Use complex prompting and quality assurance techniques.
Generate augmented retrieval and tooling.
Implement modular AI workflows using tools like LangGraph or orchestrator-worker patterns.
Integrate AI agents into existing pipelines (e.g., for NLP, geospatial, or statistical modelling tasks).
Use AI-generated outputs responsibly by applying validation techniques and human-in-the-loop review.
Monitor agent performance using defined metrics (e.g., accuracy, latency, reproducibility).

competencies.description: Business acumen in data science refers to the ability to understand and apply knowledge of business operations, strategy, and decision-making processes. It involves identifying business needs, aligning data-driven insights with organizational goals, and making decisions that drive organizational success.
indicators: Collaborate with business teams to identify key business objectives and tailor data science projects to align with those objectives.
Assess the potential impact of data science solutions on business performance and communicate how the findings can influence business decisions.
Conduct market research or competitive analysis to understand industry trends and incorporate relevant external data into business decisions.
Work with cross-functional teams (e.g., marketing, finance, product) to ensure data projects are aligned with business priorities.
Tie visualizations explicitly to business rationale and intended use.

competencies.description: Project Management in the context of data science involves planning, organizing, and overseeing data-driven projects from initiation to completion. It includes managing resources, timelines, and deliverables while ensuring that project goals align with business objectives. It also involves risk management, stakeholder communication, and iterative problem-solving throughout the project lifecycle.
indicators: Independently manage smaller, less complex tasks within a project, ensuring deadlines and deliverables are met.
Monitor the progress of data science projects, ensuring the team stays on track, and adjust when necessary (e.g., reallocating resources or extending deadlines).
Identify and mitigate moderate risks in data science projects, including technical issues, resource shortages, or data availability concerns.
Provide regular updates to stakeholders on the status of the project, ensuring clear communication of timelines, issues, and changes.
Engage with users to collect feedback/data during idea/solution implementation.
Engage in evidence-building activities throughout the project cycle.
Flag AI/data governance issues.
Adjust work based on continuous user feedback.
Register new AI solutions/projects with appropriate stakeholders.

competencies.description: Data processing refers to the collection, cleaning, transformation, and manipulation of raw data into a format suitable for analysis and decision-making. It involves handling data from various sources, ensuring its quality, and making it ready for statistical analysis or machine learning models.
indicators: Combine multiple datasets from different sources using joins or merges based on common keys, handling inconsistencies in data structure.

Process both structured data (e.g., databases, spreadsheets) and unstructured data (e.g., text, logs) for analysis.

competencies.description: Knowledge and ability to design, define, construct, enhance, support, and maintain software associated with machine learning.
indicators: Design and implement functions and classes in Python or R, applying object-oriented programming principles.
Use libraries like Pandas, NumPy, or dplyr to perform data manipulation tasks such as cleaning, transforming, and aggregating data.
Write and implement basic unit tests and functions for quality assurance.
Provide drill down functionality in visualizations.

competencies.description: Knowledge in a range of mathematical and statistical techniques, understanding and being able to apply them, and comprehending their underlying assumptions and limitations.
indicators: Apply inferential statistics such as hypothesis testing (t-tests, chi-square tests), confidence intervals, and p-values to draw conclusions from sample data.
Perform and interpret simple linear regression, including understanding the relationship between dependent and independent variables.
Apply techniques for uncovering patterns in data through visualizations and basic statistical analysis, including correlation and scatter plots.
Perform basic multivariate statistical techniques, such as multiple linear regression or principal component analysis (PCA), to handle multiple variables.
Understand the pros and cons of various statistical tests and when they should be applied.

competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

It includes anticipating and overcoming obstacles, driving projects forward, and using resourcefulness to both improve performance and promote innovation. This competency extends to encouraging experimentation and new ideas, demonstrating resilience amid change, and taking ownership for outcomes.

competencies.competency: Working Effectively with Others (Mobilize People; Collaborate with Partners and Stakeholders)

indicators: Create a sense of common purpose and direction in the organization and among colleagues.

Implement and communicate strategies that enhance collaboration.
Acknowledge the contribution of others in achieving objectives.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Ensure that standards and safeguards are in place to protect organizational integrity.

Develop data-driven narratives that directly link findings to business objectives, demonstrating how the insights impact strategy and decision-making.
Communicate risks of AI-generated content (e.g., copyright, bias, etc.).
